title: WPMS/2706/2019 of KISHORE SINGH NEGI Vs YOGESH CHANDRA UPRETI

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 2706 of 2019 (M/S)
Kishore Singh Negi ....Petitioner.
Versus
Yogesh Chandra Upreti .... Respondent.
Present :
Mr. Sarvesh Agarwal, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Rajesh Joshi, Advocate for the respondent.
 Dated: 11th March, 2020
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The present Writ Petition has been preferred by the petitioner,
being aggrieved against the order dated 12th July, 2019, as rendered by
Judge Small Cause Court / Civil Judge (Junior Division), Nainital in
SCC Case No. 2/2013, Yogesh Chandra Upreti Vs. Kishore Singh
Negi. By virtue of the order impugned rendered by the Judge Small
Causes Court in SCC Case No. 2/2013, issue No. 6 pertaining to the
implications of Section 23 of Provincial Small Causes Court Act has
been decided and, as a consequence thereto, the Judge Small Causes
Court, had held that the issue and the impact of Section 23 since it
entails an appreciation of evidence and facts too, it has to be decided
at the stage of final adjudication of the suit. It has further been
observed that when the Suit itself is being considered on its merit, it
would be at that stage which would be the appropriate stage to
consider the implication of Section 23 of Provincial Small Causes
Court Act.
2. The said order dated 12th July, 2019 of JSCC Court was
put to challenge by the petitioner by filing a SCC Revision under
Section 25 of the Provincial Small Causes Court Act and the
Revisional Court too by the impugned judgement dated 29th August,
2019, had dismissed the Revision and thereby affirmed the order
dated 12th July, 2019 whereby the following observations was made :

3. When challenge was given to the impugned order before
this Court, initially, the Court had issued notices to the respondents
without grant of interim order and thereafter a clarification of the said
order was made by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court by its order
dated 25th September, 2019 to the effect that there is no interim order
as such granted in the present Writ Petition and the Trial Court's
proceeding was directed to be carried as usual. The only
apprehension, which the petitioner has expressed that the finding,
which has been recorded pertaining to ascertainment of title on issue
No. 6, while considering the implication of Section 23, though despite
the fact that the said issue of dispute of title, it has been directed to be
considered after the parties lead their respective evidence in the
proceeding of the suit itself. In such an eventuality, where by the
impugned order, the Court has directed to consider the impact of
Section 23, at final stage itself after letting the parties to avail their
opportunity of evidence and placement of their respective case at the
stage of trial, no finding as such, which may any impact with regard to
the determination of the title of either of the parties to the Suit, ought
not to have been recorded. Since the order dated 12th July, 2019 was
only postponing the consideration of issue of title under Section 23,
which was otherwise directed to be decided at the final stage of the
suit itself, any stray finding recorded pertaining to the title of the
parties to the proceedings under Section 15 of Provincial Small Cause
Courts Act obviously will not be read or create any embargo in an
independent consideration of implication under Section 23, when
issue No. 6 itself is decided afresh by the Trial Court at the stage of

3
final adjudication of the Suit, as a consequence of order of remand
impugned in the Writ Petition.
4. Hence, this Writ Petition is being dismissed with minor
clarification to the effect that any stray finding recorded by the Trial
Court in its order dated 12th July, 2019 pertaining to the title of either
of the parties to the Suit will only be tentative expression and will not
create an embargo to prejudice the mind of the Judge Small Cause
Court, when issue No. 6 is independently decided at the stage of final
adjudication of SCC Case No. 2 of 2013 and it is directed to be
decided independently without being influenced by the finding
recorded therein, in the impugned orders.
5. Subject to the above observations and the exception as
carved out, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
6. Let copy of the order be supplied by tomorrow, i.e.
12.03.2020.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
